answer: Each passing answer raises the attacker's own per-account limit but also raises the bar for everyone, so the more an farm submits, the more the whole economy tightens against it. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a echo as the anchor of the cost.
